title: Polynomial time for countdown output
statement: Let $g,e,x,r,f$ be functions on bit strings, with $g$ the block-loop step determined by $\mathrm{upd},\mathrm{nxt}$ and $e$ the corresponding output function determined by $\mathrm{out}$. Fix a bit string $h_0$ and natural numbers $a',k',c$. Suppose the functions $s\mapsto\mathrm{upd}(\pi_1(s),\pi_2(\pi_2(s)))$, $s\mapsto\mathrm{nxt}(\pi_1(s),\pi_2(\pi_2(s)))$, $\mathrm{out}$, $x$, and $r$ are polynomial-time computable, where $\pi_1,\pi_2$ are the total projections from the self-delimiting pair parser. Suppose also that for every nonempty bit string $h$ and every bit string $q$, $2|\mathrm{upd}(h,q)|+|\mathrm{nxt}(h,q)|\le 2|h|+|q|+2+c$. If, for every bit string $z$, concatenating the outputs $e(g^{[i]}(\langle h_0,\langle 1^{a'(|x(z)|+1)^{k'}},r(z)\rangle\rangle))$ over all integers $i$ with $0\le i<a'(|x(z)|+1)^{k'}+1$ gives $f(z)$, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $e$ is the output function determined by $\mathrm{out}$
The parsed-update function is polynomial-time computable
The parsed-next function is polynomial-time computable
The stated length-growth inequality holds for every nonempty $h$ and every $q$
The specified finite concatenation equals $f(z)$ for every $z$
